correctness.rationale: For all finite connected factors without triangles or four-cycles, a same-direction neighbor pair has unique common center. Thus a face containing three or more neighbors of a center is confined to one maximal closed neighborhood and admits the stated decreasing-cardinality free-face pairing. Remaining unique-common-neighbor distance-two edges are free. The complete residue is precisely the double triangulation of every product square, with ordinary graph product 1-skeleton. One disc per square forms |H| times |J|, while each second disc is attached along a boundary already bounding a disc, and contributes S2. Exact integral homotopy follows without assuming field homology detects attaching maps. Ten finite complete face-poset replays, including C5 square C5 and C5 square C6, independently checked the free-face condition and mod-two boundaries.

evidence: The high-girth prism formula covers H Cartesian K2, yielding H wedged with |E(H)| two-spheres; this is a strictly narrower case. The clique-fiber theorem covers H Cartesian K_m for m>=3, whose second factor contains triangles, and gives a different assembly. Matsushita Example 3.5 treats K_m Cartesian K_n, with triangles in both factors. Hypercube results have tree-like factors.
broader_coverage.reasoning: No inspected stronger result includes all products of two girth-five factors. The new formula includes factors with independent cycles, where the fundamental group becomes their direct product and a Künneth H2 term appears.

originality.rationale: The whole claim is a uniform integral product-space plus one sphere per Cartesian square decomposition for two girth-at-least-five factors. The inspected closed-neighborhood general source proves only a complete-graph Cartesian example; the cube graph literature has contractible factor graphs; the published high-girth prism case H square K2 is explicitly credited as a proper special case, not novel; H square K_m with m>=3 violates factor girth; toroidal open-neighborhood complexes are different. Independent statements and stronger implications were compared, rather than relying on keyword nonmatches. An unindexed broader square-completion theorem is a real residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed general statement on closed-neighborhood complexes of square-completed graphs could imply the splitting.
Published code or a non-indexed appendix may contain the same toroidal scale-two integral homotopy result without the queried terminology.

value.rationale: This natural graph Čech family generalizes the prior high-girth prism specialization to two genuinely non-tree factors and produces a product fundamental group and a Künneth H2 term in addition to exactly one sphere per Cartesian square. The explicit elementary collapses and exact integral homotopy splitting explain local neighborhood effects on global product topology, with a motivated toroidal family C_m square C_n yielding T2 wedged with mn S2; the result is neither a numerical table entry nor a simple relabeling.
